case_name: Abhilasha Sharma And Others vs State Of H.P. And Others
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Complainant No.2's marriage was solemnized with accused No.1, but she took all valuables and did not return after 15 days. Complainants searched their house and found that valuable articles worth ₹15 lakhs were stolen.

legal_principles.principle: The Court should apply the test as to whether the uncontroverted allegations prima facie establish the offence or not.
legal_principles.held: If the allegations are so patently absurd and inherently improbable that no prudent person can ever reach such a conclusion and where the basic ingredients of a criminal offence are not satisfied then the Court may interfere.

legal_principles.principle: The Court should not unduly interfere and meticulous examination of the evidence is needed for considering whether the case would end in conviction or not at the stage of framing of charge or quashing of charge.
legal_principles.held: No meticulous examination of the evidence is needed for considering whether the case would end in conviction or not at the stage of framing of charge or quashing of charge.

legal_principles.principle: The Court has a duty to balance the freedom of a person and the right of the complainant or prosecution to investigate and prosecute the offender.
legal_principles.held: The Court has a duty to balance the freedom of a person and the right of the complainant or prosecution to investigate and prosecute the offender.

legal_principles.principle: Where the allegations made and as they appeared from the record and documents annexed therewith predominantly give rise to and constitute a 'civil wrong' with no 'element of criminality', the court may be justified in quashing the charge.
legal_principles.held: Even in such cases, the court would not embark upon the critical analysis of the evidence.
